title: NASA Calls for Proposals to Accelerate Lunar Surface Technologies
summary: NASA is seeking lunar infrastructure technology proposals. This creates a research lead for power supply and resource-production scenarios, but supplies no validated hardware performance values for the model.

reported_facts.statement: NASA announced a solicitation on September 8 for technologies supporting lunar South Pole infrastructure.
The listed areas include vertical solar arrays, oxygen production from regolith, radioisotope Stirling generators, advanced manufacturing, and nanomaterials.
reported_facts.locator: Five capability areas listed under NextSTEP-3 Appendix A

simulation_actions.rationale: The solicitation makes alternative power supply and storage architectures relevant to the base energy budget.
simulation_actions.next_step: Prepare a study comparing solar-plus-storage and a constant power-source placeholder across the same lunar illumination profile. Obtain actual power, storage, degradation and thermal inputs before executing a decision-grade comparison.
simulation_actions.acceptance_criteria: Study reports unmet load in Wh, minimum state of charge, and blackout survival time for both cases; all numerical inputs trace to sources or explicitly bounded assumptions. No design is called flight-ready.

simulation_actions.rationale: Oxygen production and manufacturing could change delivered cargo and power demand, but the announcement establishes research intent rather than operational capability.
simulation_actions.next_step: Draft a coupled oxygen-production and power-demand study. Compare imported oxygen against a regolith-processing concept and identify the production rate, duty cycle, equipment mass and energy data needed to run it.
simulation_actions.acceptance_criteria: Mass and energy balances use consistent units; the study states its break-even assumptions and cannot claim reduced resupply until sourced inputs support that result.
